clue: A reasonable but not absolute level of confidence that systems work as intended.
description: Assurance is the reasonable, not absolute, confidence an audit gives management that systems work as intended.
why: An audit can never check everything, so it promises reasonable confidence rather than a guarantee.

clue: The chance that an event will stop an organization from meeting its objectives.
description: Risk is the chance that an event stops the organization from meeting its objectives.
why: Auditors spend more time on high-risk areas such as payroll and online payments.

clue: How large or serious an error must be to change a reasonable user's decision.
description: Materiality is the size or nature of an error that would change a reasonable user's decision.
why: It tells the auditor which errors matter, so a rounding error is ignored but a missing approval is not.

clue: An ISACA framework for governing and managing enterprise IT and its control objectives.
description: COBIT is ISACA's framework for the governance and management of enterprise IT.
why: It gives auditors a shared set of control objectives that link IT processes to business goals.

clue: Splitting request, approval, and recording of a transaction among different people so no one person controls it.
description: Segregation of duties means no single person can request, approve, and record the same transaction.
why: Fraud then needs two or more people working together, which makes it much harder.

clue: Testing a selected portion of a population to draw conclusions about the whole.
description: Sampling is testing part of a population and drawing conclusions about all of it.
why: Auditors cannot check every transaction, and statistical methods show how confident they can be.

clue: Information such as logs, screenshots, and interview notes that supports an auditor's conclusion.
description: Evidence is the information an auditor collects, such as system logs, screenshots and interview notes.
why: Every audit conclusion must rest on it, and evidence the auditor produces directly is the most reliable.

clue: A chronological record of who did what in a system, and when.
description: An audit trail is a chronological record of who did what in a system, and when.
why: Without one, unauthorized changes can go unnoticed.

clue: Turning readable data into a coded form that only holders of the correct key can read.
description: Encryption turns readable data into a coded form that only people with the correct key can read.
why: It protects data even if the files or devices holding it are stolen.

clue: A regular copy of data that lets an organization recover after a failure.
description: A backup is a regular copy of data kept so the organization can restore it.
why: It lets the organization recover after a failure or a ransomware attack.
